discovery: Cooling and quantum control of molecules, opening ultracold molecular physics and precision tests of fundamental symmetries

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

nominees.name: David DeMille
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

motivation: Laser cooling of atoms was recognised in 1997, but molecules, with their rich vibrational and rotational structure, long resisted such control. The nominees overcame this. Doyle introduced buffer-gas cooling and cryogenic molecular beams; DeMille achieved the first direct laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping of a molecule (SrF); Ye, with the late Deborah Jin, produced a near-degenerate gas of ground-state polar KRb molecules and demonstrated chemical reactions controlled at the quantum level. Together these advances created ultracold molecular physics: quantum-state-resolved chemistry at nanokelvin temperatures, new platforms for quantum simulation and computing with dipolar molecules, and, through the ACME collaboration of DeMille and Doyle, the most stringent limits on the electron electric dipole moment, probing physics beyond the Standard Model at energies far beyond accelerators. This work turns the molecule, long a complication, into a precision instrument for fundamental physics.
